study type: Quality Improvement Audit (pre-post intervention) with Retrospective Review
outcome: Quality of neonatal birth asphyxia care (checking vital signs, laboratory investigations, thermal support, correct diagnosis, correct treatment, correct feeding, clinical officer ward rounds, daily weight checks)
cohort: Neonates diagnosed with birth asphyxia whose case notes were reviewed at Balaka District Hospital in Malawi.
finding: The implementation of a criterion-based audit significantly improved various aspects of quality care for neonates with birth asphyxia, including vital sign checks, lab investigations, diagnosis, treatment, and feeding practices, and also led to a decrease in neonatal mortality.
cross-section timing: Data was collected via retrospective review at two time points: an initial audit and a re-audit 6 months later.
